answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a refundable bond that is slashed when peers prove duplicate or fraudulent work. A cautionary fable warns that cheap names multiply like sparks from one ember; here each new name must post real collateral, sealed like onyx in a vault. Forging a hundred agents means locking a hundred bonds and losing them all on detection, so deception costs more than honest work earns.
